solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Detective writer nobody need say film director wanted back

indicators.note: something wanted back is asked to be returned, so the whole string is read in the opposite direction

blocks.note: to need something is to miss it
Nicolas Roeg directed Don't Look Now and Walkabout

explanation.surface: A crime novelist is told nobody wants to hear that a film director is wanted back on the project.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' is the usual crossword signal for an example, abbreviated e.g. Nicolas Roeg was a British film director; everything is joined first, then the whole chain runs backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: The Belgian novelist created Inspector Maigret, so he is a celebrated author of crime fiction featuring a police investigator.

clue.text: Stadium heralding Pat’s lob, perhaps

blocks.note: a sports stadium is a ground
a pat is a gentle stroke; the 's is 'is'

explanation.surface: At a tennis stadium, a player called Pat is about to play a lob.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heralding' just places the first piece before the second. 'Pat' looks like a person's name, but it is the verb for touching gently.
explanation.definitionFit: A lob is one kind of shot played after the ball bounces in tennis, hence 'perhaps' marking an example.

clue.text: Very serious about gross animal

indicators.note: about can mean turned round, as in an about-turn, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: po means stolid or humourless, as in po-faced
a gross is a total amount, a sum

explanation.surface: Someone grimly complains about a disgusting creature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gross' reads as disgusting but is the noun for a total. PO is an informal British adjective meaning prim and humourless, usually seen in po-faced.
explanation.definitionFit: The opossum is a marsupial of the Americas, so it is a kind of creature; the general category stands for the specific.

clue.text: Dance to jazz flute

blocks.note: first meaning: to move rhythmically to music
second meaning: a channel cut in a column or surface

explanation.surface: Someone dances along to a jazz flute solo.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flute' looks like the instrument in a jazz band, but it is the architectural term for a long channel cut into a surface.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both moving rhythmically to music and a long narrow channel, which is what a flute in a pillar is.

clue.text: Underwear – pair seen in the middle of dressing?

definitions.text: Underwear – pair seen in the middle of dressing?

blocks.note: surface reading: underclothes, seen while someone is getting dressed

blocks.clueFragment: pair seen in the middle of dressing?
blocks.note: setter's reading: the two lower-case letters at the very centre of the word 'dressing'

explanation.surface: A pair of knickers glimpsed halfway through getting dressed.
explanation.walkthrough: The middle two letters of 'dressing' are both lower-case S, so they are small esses; that same word is British slang for underclothes.
explanation.definitionFit: In British informal usage, underpants and other underclothes washed and hung out are called by this plural noun.

clue.text: Game‘s popular forward upended one defender at the start

indicators.note: in a down clue, upending turns a word on its head, so it reads bottom to top
the start of a word is its opening letter, so only that one is kept

blocks.note: one as the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: In a football match, a popular striker unexpectedly topples a defender at kick-off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Game', 'forward' and 'defender' all suggest football, but 'Game' is the adjective meaning plucky, and 'forward' means cheeky.
explanation.definitionFit: Being game means willing and brave, ready to take on a challenge, which is what a fearless person is.

clue.text: Poor inns are ultimately losing revenue

indicators.note: something poor is in bad shape, so these letters are knocked out of order
ultimately means at the very end, so only the closing letter is taken

explanation.surface: Run-down pubs are, in the end, losing money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing revenue' reads as a business failing, but 'losing' only supplies its last letter and 'revenue' stands alone as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Revenue is income received, and money earned or taken in is the plural noun meaning income.

clue.text: Graduate in Old English once called immodest

indicators.note: to be in something is to sit inside it, so one piece goes within another

blocks.note: the standard abbreviation for Old English
né, the masculine of née, used for a man's former name

explanation.surface: A scholar of Old English was once labelled shameless.
explanation.walkthrough: NE is né, the less familiar masculine form of née, meaning 'formerly called' when giving a man's earlier name.
explanation.definitionFit: Something indecent or offensive to modesty is lacking in decorum, so the adjectives are close synonyms.

clue.text: Feature added by architect d’Agnolo voluntarily when flipping houses

indicators.note: to house something is to hold it inside, so the letters are tucked within the words
flipping something turns it over, so the letters run right to left

blocks.note: the end of the name runs into the start of the next word

explanation.surface: A Renaissance architect adds a feature of his own accord while renovating houses for profit.
explanation.walkthrough: Baccio d'Agnolo was a real Florentine architect, which makes the surface convincing. 'flipping houses' reads as property dealing.
explanation.definitionFit: This rounded convex moulding, a quarter-circle in section, is a classical decorative detail used on cornices and capitals.

clue.text: Symbol put on the line by teacher apart from margins

indicators.note: margins are the edges of a page, so dropping them removes the first and last letters

blocks.note: MASTER, a schoolmaster, without its edge letters
to put something on the line is to endanger it

explanation.surface: A teacher writes a mark on a ruled line, leaving the margins clear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'teacher' must first become MASTER before its margins are trimmed. 'by' means beside, so the trimmed teacher goes next to the danger word.
explanation.definitionFit: The little star printed to flag a footnote is a typographical mark, one of many such printed characters.

clue.text: Cuckoo, crane and tit circling lake – first one’s heard in the reeds

indicators.note: cuckoo means crazy, so these letters go wild and rearrange
to circle something is to go round it, so one piece is enclosed

blocks.note: L is the abbreviation for lake
first is written 1st, with I standing for the 1

explanation.surface: A cuckoo, a crane and a tit circle a lake, and the first is heard calling from the reed beds.
explanation.walkthrough: The birds fit the reed-bed scene, but 'Cuckoo' means mad and 'reeds' is the reed section of an orchestra.
explanation.definitionFit: Woodwind players of single-reed instruments sit in the orchestra's reed section, so this performer is heard among them.

clue.text: Remains in Nevada before using final bits of annual leave east of Illinois’s state capital

indicators.note: to be in something is to sit inside it, so one piece is enclosed by another
the final bit of each word is its last letter, so only those are kept

blocks.note: the US postal code for Nevada
the US postal code for Illinois

explanation.surface: Someone's ashes rest in Nevada before they take holiday in Illinois's capital city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'east of' places the letters after the Illinois abbreviation in an across clue. The state capital of Illinois is Springfield, a false trail: the possessive only links wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Tennessee's seat of government is this city, famous for country music, so it is one of the American state capitals.

clue.text: Complete clue alongside learner

blocks.note: a clue gives an idea, a hint
L for learner, as on L-plates

explanation.surface: A finished crossword clue sits next to a novice solver.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Complete' looks like a verb telling you to finish the clue, but it is the adjective meaning perfect.
explanation.definitionFit: Something perfect in every respect, lacking nothing, can be called complete, as in a complete gentleman.

clue.text: Twin son, not yet 12, heading for Europe

indicators.note: the heading of a word is its opening letter, so just that one is taken

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: One of a pair of twin boys, not yet twelve years old, sets off for Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not yet 12' reads as an age but means a time of day: before noon. 'Twin' is an adjective here, as in twin beds.
explanation.definitionFit: Twin things are identical, matching each other exactly, so the adjective works as a synonym.

clue.text: Literary work e.g. Larkin composed

indicators.note: to compose is to put together, so these letters are arranged afresh

explanation.surface: A piece of writing, for example one Philip Larkin wrote.
explanation.walkthrough: Larkin was an English poet, so the surface reads as a book he wrote; the answer is instead Shakespeare's tragedy.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's tragedy about an old king and his three daughters is a famous piece of literature.

clue.text: Pope Leo, essentially good man, most civilised

indicators.note: the essence of something is its core, so the central letter is taken

blocks.note: Urban is the name of eight popes
a good man is a saint, ST

explanation.surface: Pope Leo is praised as fundamentally a good man and the most refined of all.
explanation.walkthrough: Leo is also a papal name, which makes 'Pope Leo' look like one person; the pope is a different one and Leo only gives its middle letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Urbane means suave and polished in manner, so its superlative describes the most refined, courteous person.

clue.text: House not quite finished in current advanced state

indicators.note: something not quite finished stops just short of its end, so the last letter goes

blocks.note: Virgo is a house of the zodiac, cut short
I is the symbol for electric current
A is the abbreviation for advanced

explanation.surface: An unfinished house stands in an advanced state of decay at present.
explanation.walkthrough: 'House' is an astrological house, one of the twelve zodiac signs. 'advanced state' reads as a condition, but 'state' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: This is one of the fifty United States, on the Atlantic coast, so it fits the noun for a federal division.

clue.text: Stay in lounge prior to shower

blocks.note: to lounge is to rest idly

explanation.surface: Someone stays in the lounge before taking a shower.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stay in' looks like a phrasal verb about remaining indoors, but 'Stay' alone is the definition, in the sense of holding back.
explanation.definitionFit: To stay someone's hand is to check or hold it back, as in staying an execution, so the verbs match.

clue.text: Singer performing rap and so on

indicators.note: performing means putting on an act, so these letters are worked into a new form

explanation.surface: A vocalist performs rap music and similar styles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'and' simply joins the two pieces of letters to be rearranged together.
explanation.definitionFit: The soprano is the highest female or boy's voice, and the term also names the vocalist with that range.

clue.text: Settlement in Scotland: ordinary embargo follows

blocks.note: O for ordinary, as in O level

explanation.surface: A Scottish village faces an ordinary trade embargo.
explanation.walkthrough: 'follows' places the ban after the abbreviation for ordinary.
explanation.definitionFit: Oban is a port town on the west coast of Argyll, the gateway to the Hebridean ferries, so it is a Scottish settlement.

clue.text: Some disliked a Corbynite’s regressive material

indicators.note: some of a phrase is only part of it, so the letters lie inside the words
to regress is to go backwards, so the letters are read right to left

blocks.note: the end of the first word runs across the middle word into the start of the last

explanation.surface: Some people dislike a Labour leftist's backward-looking manifesto.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regressive' fits the political surface but is the signal to read backwards. A Corbynite is a follower of Jeremy Corbyn, former Labour Party leader.
explanation.definitionFit: Brocade is a rich woven fabric with a raised pattern, often in silk, so it is a kind of cloth.

clue.text: Tight Pointless

blocks.note: second meaning: to no purpose, futile

explanation.walkthrough: 'Tight' looks like it means taut or stingy; here it is slang for drunk, and the answer is equally slang for that state.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is slang for very drunk and also describes effort spent in vain, achieving nothing useful.

clue.text: See you bagging rubbish without thinking

indicators.note: to bag something is to put it inside a bag, so one piece holds another

explanation.surface: Someone says goodbye while bagging up rubbish mindlessly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rubbish' suggests refuse being bagged, but it means nonsense.
explanation.definitionFit: Learning by mechanical repetition rather than understanding is done mindlessly, through memory and habit alone.

clue.text: With a lot of outrage post Greek’s last letter to Athenians

indicators.note: a lot of something is most but not all of it, so the final letter goes
the last of a word is its final letter, so only that one is kept

blocks.note: APPAL, to outrage, minus its tail

explanation.surface: A furious letter is sent to the people of Athens after a Greek's last word.
explanation.walkthrough: 'post' means after, so the shortened outrage comes after the Greek's last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Kappa is the tenth character of the Greek alphabet, so it is a letter that people in Athens would use.

clue.text: Part of the service that includes some Browning?

definitions.text: Part of the service that includes some Browning?

blocks.clueFragment: Part of the service that includes some Browning?
blocks.note: surface reading: a church service with a reading from the poet Robert Browning
setter's reading: gravy browning, a colouring sauce, held in a jug that is part of a dinner service

explanation.surface: A church service includes a reading of a Robert Browning poem.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital B steers you to the poet; really 'service' is a set of crockery and browning is the British sauce colouring used in gravy.
explanation.definitionFit: The jug for pouring meat sauce at table belongs to a dinner set, and holds liquid darkened with browning.

clue.text: Film fan biting large piece of noisette?

definitions.note: noisette is French for this nut, so the question mark flags a definition by example

indicators.note: something biting holds a morsel in its jaws, so it surrounds another piece

blocks.note: L is the abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: A cinema fan bites into a big piece of chocolate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Film fan' reads as a cinema lover, but the two words are separate pieces, and together they grip the large.
explanation.definitionFit: Noisette is a paste or praline flavoured with the kernel of the cob tree, so that kernel is one part of it.

clue.text: African resident‘s tax paid regularly after fine

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter is kept

explanation.surface: An African householder's taxes are paid on time after a fine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' puts the alternate letters behind the word for fine. 'resident' sounds like a person, but the definition is an animal.
explanation.definitionFit: The okapi is a forest mammal related to the giraffe, native only to the Congo, so it lives in Africa.

clue.text: Strengthening mix of fortified wine left with church staff close to transept

indicators.note: the close of a word is its end, so only its final letter is taken

explanation.surface: A fortifying drink of port is left with the church staff near the transept.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fortified' and 'Strengthening' suggest the wine, but the definition is a building material. CE is the Church of England; the transept is the cross-arm of a church.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the commonest building binder, mixed with sand and water to make concrete that strengthens structures.
